```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(DT)

source("functions.R")
refined_dir <- "simulations/refined"
refined_summary <- load_and_summarize_simulations(refined_dir)

# `overall_power`/`pos_power`/`length_power` (semanticprimeR::calculate_correction)
# record, for each dataset run (and, for the subgroup tables, each group
# within that run), the *achieved* percent_below nearest each requested
# power level (a near-continuous number like 76.85, not a clean 80) - but
# always in the fixed order of REFINE_POWER_LEVELS below, up to six rows
# per run/group (fewer if the search window didn't reach the higher
# levels - percent_below is monotonic in sample_size, so any missing
# levels are always the highest ones, never a gap in the middle).
# Grouping directly on the raw percent_below value treats every run's
# slightly-different achieved value as its own bin, so pools across runs
# barely happen. Binning by position within each run recovers the
# intended target instead.
REFINE_POWER_LEVELS <- c(70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95)
TARGET_POWER <- 80
TARGET_RELIABILITY <- 0.80
```

```{r helpers}
label_by_target <- function(power_tbl, group_vars = "run_id", power_levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS) {
  power_tbl %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(group_vars))) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(target_power = power_levels[((dplyr::row_number() - 1) %% length(power_levels)) + 1]) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}

summarize_by_target <- function(power_tbl, group_vars = "run_id", power_levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS) {
  label_by_target(power_tbl, group_vars, power_levels) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(target_power) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n_runs = sum(!is.na(corrected_sample_size)),
      mean_recommended_sample_size = mean(corrected_sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_recommended_sample_size = median(corrected_sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_recommended_sample_size = sd(corrected_sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
      min_recommended_sample_size = min(corrected_sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_recommended_sample_size = max(corrected_sample_size, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(target_power) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(recommended_sample_size = ceiling(cummax(median_recommended_sample_size)))
}

# Standard 1.5x IQR rule. Applied separately to the precision-recommended
# and reliability-recommended sample sizes for a group, so a handful of
# very small/noisy source datasets (which can swing corrected_sample_size
# or the reliability-hit sample size wildly) don't dominate the average.
IQR_MULTIPLIER <- 1.5

iqr_bounds <- function(x, multiplier = IQR_MULTIPLIER) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) < 4) return(c(lower = -Inf, upper = Inf))
  qs <- stats::quantile(x, probs = c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE, type = 7)
  iqr <- qs[[2]] - qs[[1]]
  c(lower = qs[[1]] - multiplier * iqr, upper = qs[[2]] + multiplier * iqr)
}

n_at_precision_per_run <- function(power_tbl, group_vars = "run_id", target_power = TARGET_POWER) {
  label_by_target(power_tbl, group_vars) %>%
    dplyr::filter(target_power == !!target_power) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(run_id, n_precision = corrected_sample_size)
}

# Reliability is never estimated below n = 20 (see run_simulation_pipeline() /
# run_simulation_pipeline_chunked() in functions.R), so the sample size at
# which a run first hits the reliability target is naturally floored at 20 -
# even a dataset that happens to hit 80% reliability at very small n can't
# pull this metric below the floor.
n_at_reliability_per_run <- function(rel_tbl, target_reliability = TARGET_RELIABILITY) {
  rel_tbl %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      reliability_m = as.numeric(reliability_m),
      sample_size = as.numeric(sample_size)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(reliability_m)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(run_id) %>%
    dplyr::filter(reliability_m >= target_reliability) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(sample_size) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(run_id, n_reliability = sample_size)
}

# For one group (Overall, a POS tag, or a length bucket): per-run n needed
# for target_power% precision and for target_reliability split-half
# reliability, IQR-outlier-trimmed separately, then averaged together into
# a single recommended sample size.
summarize_group_recommendation <- function(power_tbl, rel_tbl,
                                           target_power = TARGET_POWER,
                                           target_reliability = TARGET_RELIABILITY) {
  precision_per_run <- n_at_precision_per_run(power_tbl, target_power = target_power)
  reliability_per_run <- n_at_reliability_per_run(rel_tbl, target_reliability = target_reliability)

  precision_bounds <- iqr_bounds(precision_per_run$n_precision)
  reliability_bounds <- iqr_bounds(reliability_per_run$n_reliability)

  per_run <- precision_per_run %>%
    dplyr::full_join(reliability_per_run, by = "run_id") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      precision_outlier = is.finite(n_precision) &
        (n_precision < precision_bounds[["lower"]] | n_precision > precision_bounds[["upper"]]),
      reliability_outlier = is.finite(n_reliability) &
        (n_reliability < reliability_bounds[["lower"]] | n_reliability > reliability_bounds[["upper"]])
    )

  precision_clean <- per_run$n_precision[is.finite(per_run$n_precision) & !per_run$precision_outlier]
  reliability_clean <- per_run$n_reliability[is.finite(per_run$n_reliability) & !per_run$reliability_outlier]

  precision_median <- stats::median(precision_clean)
  reliability_median <- stats::median(reliability_clean)

  list(
    per_run = per_run,
    precision_n_total = nrow(precision_per_run),
    precision_n_kept = length(precision_clean),
    precision_median = precision_median,
    reliability_n_total = nrow(reliability_per_run),
    reliability_n_kept = length(reliability_clean),
    reliability_median = reliability_median,
    recommended_n = mean(c(precision_median, reliability_median))
  )
}

# Renders the table/plot/recommendation block for one group (Overall, a
# POS tag, or a length bucket) - shared by the Overall/POS/Length sections
# below so the reporting logic only has to be written once.
render_group_section <- function(label, power_tbl, rel_tbl, group_vars = "run_id") {
  n_runs <- dplyr::n_distinct(power_tbl$run_id)
  cat(sprintf("Based on %d dataset run(s).\n\n", n_runs))

  if (n_runs == 0) {
    cat("No data available for this group.\n\n---\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  target_summary <- summarize_by_target(power_tbl, group_vars = group_vars)
  labeled_power <- label_by_target(power_tbl, group_vars = group_vars)

  cat("**Recommended sample size per item, by target precision (% of simulations hitting the AIPE cutoff):**\n\n")
  print(htmltools::tagList(DT::datatable(
    target_summary %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))),
    rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10)
  )))

  box_dat <- labeled_power %>%
    dplyr::mutate(target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS))
  print(
    ggplot2::ggplot(box_dat, ggplot2::aes(x = target_power, y = corrected_sample_size)) +
      ggplot2::geom_boxplot(fill = "#d9e7ff", outlier.alpha = 0.2, width = 0.6) +
      ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.35, size = 1.4) +
      ggplot2::geom_line(
        data = target_summary %>% dplyr::mutate(target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS)),
        ggplot2::aes(x = target_power, y = recommended_sample_size, group = 1),
        color = "#b00020", linewidth = 0.9
      ) +
      ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = target_summary %>% dplyr::mutate(target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS)),
        ggplot2::aes(x = target_power, y = recommended_sample_size),
        color = "#b00020", size = 2.5
      ) +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = "Target precision (%)", y = "Corrected sample size",
        title = paste0(label, ": spread of per-dataset recommendations"),
        subtitle = "red line = across-run running max of the median"
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  )

  rec <- summarize_group_recommendation(power_tbl, rel_tbl)

  if (nrow(rel_tbl) > 0) {
    cat("\n\n**Reliability by sample size (median across runs):**\n\n")
    rel_curve <- rel_tbl %>%
      dplyr::mutate(sample_size = as.numeric(sample_size), reliability_m = as.numeric(reliability_m)) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(sample_size) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(median_reliability = median(reliability_m, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

    print(
      ggplot2::ggplot(rel_curve, ggplot2::aes(x = sample_size, y = median_reliability)) +
        ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8, color = "#1f4e79") +
        ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = TARGET_RELIABILITY, linetype = "dashed", color = "#b00020") +
        ggplot2::labs(
          x = "Sample size", y = "Median split-half reliability",
          title = paste0(label, ": reliability curve across dataset runs"),
          subtitle = sprintf("dashed line = %.0f%% target", TARGET_RELIABILITY * 100)
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme_minimal()
    )
  }

  cat(sprintf(
    "\n\n**Recommended n (%d%% precision + %d%% reliability, IQR-trimmed medians averaged): %.1f -> %d participants/item**\n\n",
    TARGET_POWER, TARGET_RELIABILITY * 100, rec$recommended_n, ceiling(rec$recommended_n)
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    "- Precision: %.1f (median of %d/%d runs kept after IQR trim)\n",
    rec$precision_median, rec$precision_n_kept, rec$precision_n_total
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    "- Reliability: %.1f (median of %d/%d runs kept after IQR trim)\n",
    rec$reliability_median, rec$reliability_n_kept, rec$reliability_n_total
  ))

  cat("\n\n**Per-dataset detail (n at target precision, n at target reliability, outlier flags):**\n\n")
  print(htmltools::tagList(DT::datatable(
    rec$per_run %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(n_precision, n_reliability), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_precision)),
    rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10)
  )))

  cat("\n\n---\n")

  rec
}
```

## Sample Size Estimation for Familiarity Norming

We applied the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) and Monte Carlo
simulation procedure described by Buchanan et al. (2026) to estimate
sample sizes for familiarity ratings across published psycholinguistic
norming datasets. The procedure uses existing norming data to simulate
the number of participants needed for items to be considered
"well measured" - that is, for their standard errors (SEs) to fall
below a data-driven criterion. All analyses were carried out in R using
the `semanticprimeR` package. The full methodology is documented in
`README.md`; in brief:

1. **Simulate from known population norms.** For each dataset, we drew
   `n_per_item` observations per item from a truncated normal
   distribution, using each dataset's reported item-level means and
   standard deviations. 43 datasets were processed, spanning norming
   studies published between 1975 and 2025 across 16 languages.
2. **Pilot, then refine.** A coarse pilot sweep (sample sizes 20-500,
   step 10, 10 simulations/step) located roughly where each dataset's
   precision curve crosses 70% and 95%. A narrower, high-precision
   refine stage (step 5, 100 simulations/step) then reran the
   simulation within that dataset-specific window. **This document
   reads the refined-stage output only**, since that is the
   higher-precision, final estimate.
3. **Precision.** At each sample size, we calculated the SE for each
   item and the proportion of items whose SE fell below the 4th-decile
   cutoff, then applied a correction factor (following Buchanan et al.)
   to account for the known upward bias introduced by small pilot
   samples. Sample size recommendations are derived at four
   power-analogue thresholds - 80%, 85%, 90%, 95% of items meeting the
   SE criterion.
4. **Reliability.** Split-half reliability (participants per item split
   in half, half-means correlated, Spearman-Brown corrected) was
   calculated at each sample size, starting at *n* = 20 regardless of
   where the precision search window began, so the reliability curve
   never drops below a floor of 20 raters per item.
5. **POS and word length splits.** Each dataset was additionally split
   by part-of-speech (UDPipe-tagged) and word length prior to
   simulation, to check whether recommendations vary by lexical class.

## Target Criteria and Outlier Handling

We target `r TARGET_POWER`% power (AIPE precision) and
`r TARGET_RELIABILITY * 100`% split-half reliability, and report the
recommended sample size as the average of those two numbers. Precision
and reliability answer different questions about the same design (how
accurately measured is the estimated mean vs. how consistent are the
item scores), so averaging them gives one practical number rather than
always taking the stricter of the two. Reliability is only ever
estimated starting at *n* = 20 (see `functions.R`), so even a dataset
that happens to reach the reliability target at a very small sample
size cannot pull the recommended sample size below 20.

Each of these numbers is computed per dataset run (i.e., per source
paper/corpus) before pooling: every dataset run contributes one
"n needed for `r TARGET_POWER`% precision" value and one
"n needed for `r TARGET_RELIABILITY * 100`% reliability" value. A
handful of source datasets are small, noisy, or otherwise unusual and
can pull these per-run numbers to extreme highs or lows. Before pooling
across runs, we drop outlier runs using the standard 1.5 x IQR rule
(values more than 1.5 interquartile ranges below Q1 or above Q3 are
dropped), applied separately to the precision values and the
reliability values. We then take the median of the remaining runs for
each metric (median rather than mean, since a handful of runs can still
sit near the outlier boundary without being dropped outright - in
practice the two are close once outliers are trimmed, but median is the
more standard choice for a "typical" recommendation). The tables below
show which runs were considered outliers.

## Loading Refined Results

```{r load-results, results='asis'}
cat(sprintf(
  "Loaded refined output for **%d dataset run(s)**.\n\n",
  dplyr::n_distinct(refined_summary$overall_power$run_id)
))
```

Each dataset contributes one simulation "run" (i.e., one row per source
paper/corpus that reported familiarity for the words in our stimuli
set). The results below pool across *all* dataset runs, since our own
norming study will draw one sample of participants per item.

## Overall Results

```{r overall-results, results='asis'}
overall_rec <- render_group_section(
  "Overall",
  refined_summary$overall_power,
  refined_summary$overall_rel
)
```

## Results by Part of Speech {.tabset}

```{r pos-results, results='asis'}
pos_groups <- sort(unique(refined_summary$pos_power$group))
pos_rec_by_group <- purrr::map(pos_groups, function(g) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### %s\n\n", g))
  render_group_section(
    paste0("POS: ", g),
    refined_summary$pos_power %>% dplyr::filter(group == g),
    refined_summary$pos_rel %>% dplyr::filter(group == g)
  )
}) %>% setNames(pos_groups)
```

## Results by Word Length {.tabset}

```{r length-results, results='asis'}
length_levels <- c("3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9", "10", "11+")
length_groups <- length_levels[length_levels %in% unique(refined_summary$length_power$group)]

length_rec_by_group <- purrr::map(length_groups, function(g) {
  cat(sprintf("\n### %s letters\n\n", g))
  render_group_section(
    paste0("Length: ", g),
    refined_summary$length_power %>% dplyr::filter(group == g),
    refined_summary$length_rel %>% dplyr::filter(group == g)
  )
}) %>% setNames(length_groups)
```

## Comparison Across Subgroups

The POS and word-length breakdowns above are exploratory: they show
whether any lexical class needs a *different* number of raters than the
study as a whole, not a number to combine with the overall estimate.
The chart below compares each subgroup's recommended n against the
overall recommendation.

```{r comparison-table}
comparison_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(category = "Overall", group = "Overall", recommended_n = overall_rec$recommended_n),
  purrr::imap_dfr(pos_rec_by_group, ~ tibble::tibble(category = "POS", group = .y, recommended_n = .x$recommended_n)),
  purrr::imap_dfr(length_rec_by_group, ~ tibble::tibble(category = "Length", group = .y, recommended_n = .x$recommended_n))
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(recommended_n = round(recommended_n, 1))

DT::datatable(comparison_tbl, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 20))
```

```{r comparison-plot, fig.height=6}
comparison_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = rev(c("Overall", pos_groups, length_groups)))) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = group, y = recommended_n, fill = category)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = overall_rec$recommended_n, linetype = "dashed", color = "#b00020") +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Recommended sample size per item", fill = NULL,
    title = "Recommended sample size: overall vs. subgroups",
    subtitle = "dashed line = overall recommendation"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

The plot below overlays every subgroup's precision curve (recommended
sample size at each target precision level,
`r paste(REFINE_POWER_LEVELS, collapse = "/")`%) on two panels - all
POS tags on the left, all word-length buckets on the right - so
subgroups within each category can be compared directly against each
other, with the overall curve repeated as a dashed grey reference in
both panels. If POS and word length don't matter much for sample size
planning, the colored curves should stay tightly bunched around their
dashed reference.

```{r subgroup-curves, fig.height=6, fig.width=12}
library(patchwork)

overall_curve <- summarize_by_target(refined_summary$overall_power) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS))

pos_curves <- purrr::map_dfr(pos_groups, function(g) {
  summarize_by_target(refined_summary$pos_power %>% dplyr::filter(group == g)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = g)
}) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS),
    group = factor(group, levels = pos_groups)
  )

length_curves <- purrr::map_dfr(length_groups, function(g) {
  summarize_by_target(refined_summary$length_power %>% dplyr::filter(group == g)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = g)
}) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    target_power = factor(target_power, levels = REFINE_POWER_LEVELS),
    group = factor(group, levels = length_groups)
  )

shared_y <- range(c(overall_curve$recommended_sample_size,
                     pos_curves$recommended_sample_size,
                     length_curves$recommended_sample_size), na.rm = TRUE)

subgroup_curve_plot <- function(dat, title, legend_title) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(dat, ggplot2::aes(x = target_power, y = recommended_sample_size, group = group)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(
      data = overall_curve,
      ggplot2::aes(x = target_power, y = recommended_sample_size, group = 1),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      color = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(color = group), linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.85) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = group), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.85) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = shared_y) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = "Target precision (%)", y = "Recommended sample size",
      title = title, color = legend_title
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

pos_plot <- subgroup_curve_plot(pos_curves, " ", "POS")
length_plot <- subgroup_curve_plot(length_curves, " ", "Length")

(pos_plot | length_plot)

#  )

ggsave(

)
```

```{r bottom-line, results='asis'}
subgroup_max <- comparison_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(category != "Overall") %>%
  dplyr::filter(recommended_n == max(recommended_n, na.rm = TRUE))

cat(sprintf(
  "Bottom line: averaging %d%% precision and %d%% reliability (after dropping outlier dataset runs via the 1.5 x IQR rule) puts the overall recommended sample size at **%d participants per item**. The most demanding subgroup is %s (%s), at %.1f participants/item; every other subgroup falls at or below that.\n",
  TARGET_POWER, TARGET_RELIABILITY * 100, ceiling(overall_rec$recommended_n),
  subgroup_max$group[[1]], subgroup_max$category[[1]], subgroup_max$recommended_n[[1]]
))
```
